A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same research work, Rank-One Modified Value Iteration. The main text, algorithms, equations, nine figures, Table 1, and Appendices A–B are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of planning and learning algorithms on Garnet and Graph MDPs, plus Gridworld and policy-performance experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulation results in Section 5 and Appendix B, including convergence errors, reducible-MDP experiments, and policy-performance comparisons.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 corrects R1-QL's distribution update: v1 reads the previous distribution at sampled successors, whereas v3 accumulates source probability mass at those successors before mixing and normalizing. This implements the matrix update already stated in v1. The rank-one framework, Q-value update, and R1-VI procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate planning and learning on Garnet and Graph MDPs and planning on Absorbing and Terminal Gridworld. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding planning comparisons retain VI, PI, Nesterov-VI, and Anderson-VI; learning comparisons retain QL, Speedy QL, and Zap QL. Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and appendix experiments.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain unchanged, including Garnet's 200 states, five actions and branching factor 10, discount-factor sweeps, Anderson memory one, synchronous sampling, learning-rate schedule, 5000 learning iterations, and error thresholds. No experimental rerun or protocol revision accompanies the algorithm correction.

E4.justification: Appendix B retains the same error-trajectory analyses, reducible-Gridworld comparisons, and policy-performance analyses. The discount-factor sensitivity and convergence diagnostics already appear in v1; no new ablation or robustness evidence is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report 25 Garnet realizations, five learning seeds, and the same median and quantile-band reporting practices in Section 5 and Appendix B.2. No uncertainty-estimation procedure or run-count disclosure changes.

E6.justification: Figures 1–9 retain identical plot content, and the reported numerical and qualitative findings remain unchanged. This includes faster value convergence and matching R1-VI/VI and R1-QL/QL policy performance. No revised results are supplied for the corrected Algorithm 2.

T1.justification: Section 4 removes v1's Equation (18), whose componentwise update does not implement the preceding transposed-matrix product, and replaces it with correct accumulation pseudocode for F_k^T d_hat_{k-1}. This corrects a mathematical equivalence; theorem statements and Appendix A proofs remain unchanged apart from numbering.

C1.justification: Both versions claim rank-one modifications for planning and learning, convergence guarantees and computational complexity comparable to VI/QL, and faster empirical value convergence. The abstract and contribution list retain the same scientific scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of discount-factor behavior and reduced variance remain unchanged. Both retain limitations concerning unchanged policy-convergence speed, zero-reward absorbing states, function approximation, asynchronous learning, and unproved average-cost extensions.

D1.justification: v3 removes Section 5's statement that the supplementary material includes a Python package implementing the algorithms and experiments. Section 4 also supplies explicit matrix-product computation pseudocode. These change reproducibility documentation; the PDFs do not establish whether code was actually withdrawn.

R1.justification: The same 36 references and positioning relative to acceleration, quasi-policy iteration, operator splitting, and deflation are retained. Bibliographic capitalization corrections do not change the cited works or research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording corrections, reorganizes the presentation of definitions in Section 2, and revises the distribution-update explanation in Section 4. Affiliations and correspondence information change, and acknowledgements move to the first page. The overall section structure remains stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds a standalone pseudocode display in Section 4, reformats definitions and multiline equations, and adjusts figure spacing and reference placement. Figures 1–9 and Table 1 retain their content and visual designs.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves the inconsistency between R1-QL's stated matrix recursion and its componentwise implementation in Section 4 and Algorithm 2, improving mathematical consistency and implementability. This limited gain is tempered by removal of the supplementary Python-package availability statement. The retained convergence proofs and experimental results provide no additional validation of the corrected pseudocode.
